I made this as a campaign goal/plot point for my group. A lot of work and planning went in to it, so I thought I would put it up for your use or enjoyment. This mission/goal represents about 2 months of gaming and 18 months of hard work in-game time.

Base: Custom - New Sith Wars long range Greater Kandosii Dreadnaught -"Grat'ua" (Vengance)

Thought destroyed in the seventh battle of Ruusan, it was the primary reinforcement and the last of the Great Dreadnaughts built by Mandalore before the culture shift toward peace and abandoning the warrior culture. A Master Salvager and Military Historian/Archaeologist Shen Chahadeh uncovered a Sith picket ship in the Galactic Scrapyard with an intact flight recorder. Always curious, he decrypted it and analyzed the data. In doing so, he discovered a startling revelation: The Kandosii was exiting the battle when struck by a massive coordinated torpedo strike. Data shows though heavily damaged, it did jump to hyperspace, and recorded the coordinates of the jump. After carefully reconstructing star charts he determined it would travel unhindered until it would brush the Maw in it's jump path, likely dragging it out of hyperspace. 4 years of searching paid off, he discovered the ghost ship. With a small but competent group of trusted mercenaries, he cleaned out the various space-borne inhabitants that had taken up residence consisting of 1 giant Space Worm (exogorth) that moved in to the blast hole, a swarm of Crimson Slugs in the ship itself, and a space wasp hunting the worm. Now the ship has been moved via hyperspace tug to a hidden location near Sullust, where it has had the hull sealed and the ship refurbished into a heavily armed space station servicing the underworld as a dock and ship facility. At this time, it is speculated by the best ship engineers that it will never move under it's own power again. Engines and reactors are intact (and powering the guns and facilities), but massive superstructure damage means the engines would tear it to pieces. A tremendous effort and expense would have to be undrtaken at a full shipyard in order to make it fully operational again.

This is particularly worrying:

"Genome editing has generated controversy, with unconfirmed reports of its use in human embryos. Some scientists have expressed concern that the technique might be used by fertility doctors to edit the genes of human embryos before its safety is established (see also E. Lanphier et al. Nature 519, 410–411; 2015).":

Yes, I've read about investigations of such stories before. All that I can say is that it 'most likely' that such things haven't happened. Not definitively disproved but highly unlikely. Given the state of the art in the general scientific literature I don't think that some person is more advanced than the general medical community.

You know, although neither one of us knows the truth, I'd say it actually a lot more likely that is it true, given that many extremely well-off and secretive people are very motivated to secretly act on it before it's ready -- it's one of the most powerful drives to give every advantage to your offspring.

No doubt many would have the motive. Still, it is incompatible with the general way in which scientific research is conducted. Outside the field of military research concealment is detrimental to a scientist's career. Publicity, as much as possible, priority in publication, These and other public things are what advances a scientific career. If somebody offers a supposed secret 'miracle fix' to a rich enough purchaser the most likely thing is that the rich person will be 'sharked'.
